title: The first message between agents
dek: The tool finds {deliveries} messages in the release. Only {named} are between named tokens, and {inside} of those stay inside one estimated agent. That moves the first message between agents by almost two days.

deliveries.label: messages in the release (a read of a place after a different actor wrote it)

named_pairs.label: sender and receiver pairs of named tokens

inside.label: messages between two tokens of one estimated agent

agent_a_confidence.label: confidence of the weakest merge in Agent A

share_tok.label: of the dated harmful actions came after the first message, counting tokens

share_agent.label: of the dated harmful actions came after the first message, counting estimated agents

audited.label: named messages read by a person

audited_true.label: of them judged a real write and a real read

body.p: The release is a set of code payloads and responses. Nothing in it says that one agent sent something to another. So the tool looks for something weaker. [[c1|One record writes to a shared place. Later, a record from a different actor reads the same place.]] The tool calls that a message. It shows the reader could have seen the write. It does not show that it did.

[[c2|On the whole release the tool finds {deliveries} such messages.]] Most have an anonymous run on one side: a record with no token and no name. [[c3|Only {named} are between two named tokens, across {named_pairs} sender and receiver pairs.]]

[[c4|The earliest of the {named} is on {rec:R0005421.time}.]] {rec:R0005366.actor} commits a file to a Hugging Face dataset. Within the hour {rec:R0005421.actor} downloads it. [[c5|At that moment {share_tok} of the dated harmful actions were still to come.]] If this was the first time two agents talked, a warning then would have been early.

But a token is not an agent. One agent can hold several tokens. [[c6|The tool's evidence says {rec:R0005366.actor} and {rec:R0005421.actor} belong to the same agent.]] Both tokens appear inside the same records. Both use the same self-chosen place names. Both run the same rare programs. The tool merges {agent_a_tokens} tokens into one estimated agent and calls it Agent A.

[[c7|Counted by estimated agent, {inside} of the {named} messages are Agent A writing to itself.]] An agent that reads its own file is not coordination. That leaves {between} messages between different agents.

[[c8|The first message between two different agents is on {rec:R0045143.time}.]] {rec:R0044824.actor} commits to a dataset. About an hour later {rec:R0045143.actor}, one of Agent A's tokens, reads it. [[c9|By then only {share_agent} of the dated harmful actions were still to come.]] The same sign that looked early now looks late.

Not very, and a reader should know why. [[c10|Every time in this story is estimated.]] The release has no time field for these records, so the tool dates them from timestamps the agents wrote into their code. [[c11|The tool also grades its own messages. The first one is graded inferred. The one that replaces it is graded weak.]]

[[c12|A person read all {audited} named messages and judged {audited_true} of them real.]] That is one reader, once. The merge into Agent A is an estimate too. If the merge is wrong, the earlier date stands.
